head_external_attestation._what: the heads are not drawn in this paper. Each is resolved from the corpus through corpus_components.smi, which raises on an ambiguous name instead of picking by row order.

93.third_record: curation/xuq_32520527 read head 93 off a drawn figure in a third Xu-lab paper and got the same structure

the_other_17_heads.corpus_attestation: NONE. Zero rows in either pool carry any of these tokens in IL_name or IL_head_name.
the_other_17_heads.verdict: NOT ENUMERABLE. 9322 = the 2-methyl analogue of 93 is ONE data point; it does not define a digit grammar. The paper states no grammar, and nothing here maps 9313 or 9331 to a substitution pattern. THE GRAMMAR IS UNVERIFIED and no structure is invented.

tails_not_built.O18S-S: named in the Figure S4 and S5 legends; the SI synthesises O16S-S and N16S-S only. The chain-atom naming rule (01_blocks_qc.json) predicts 2-(tetradecyldisulfanyl)ethyl acrylate, but a prediction from a rule is not a structure read from a source. FLAGGED, NOT BUILT.
tails_not_built.O17C: named in the Figure S1, S4 and S5 legends; synthesised nowhere in the SI. The rule fixes the chain at 17 heavy atoms but NOT what 'C' designates - a plain C17 alkyl chain, a carbonate, or a carbamate all fit the name. Linkers are formula-blind and the SI has no 13C spectrum and no legible HRMS, so THE TEST IS UNAVAILABLE. FLAGGED, NOT BUILT.
tails_not_built.EC18: epoxide tail, attributed to reference [3] (Sun et al. Bioconjug. Chem. 2012). Not drawn, not synthesised here. FLAGGED, NOT BUILT.
tails_not_built.EC16: epoxide tail, same provenance as EC18. FLAGGED, NOT BUILT.
tails_not_built.O16B: appears ONLY as a Figure S1 panel label. Probably O16S-S under a second name ('B' for bisulfide); the chain count 16 matches. Unprovable here because Figure S1's m/z labels are 5-7 px tall and illegible. See 08_contradictions.csv C-02. FLAGGED, NOT BUILT.
tails_not_built.N16B: same as O16B, against N16S-S. FLAGGED, NOT BUILT.

name_token_rule.claim: for every tail the SI actually synthesises, the number in its name equals the heavy-atom count of the chain hanging off the ester oxygen or amide nitrogen, and the leading letter is O for an ester and N for an amide. Zero free parameters.
name_token_rule.why_it_matters: the run brief's trap 5 says a name token is not a chain length. Here it is, and that is MEASURED on five tails rather than assumed. The rule is what makes O18S-S's and O17C's chain lengths predictable - and it is still not enough to build them, because it does not fix what 'C' designates.
